newsitem.title: INDIA: RBI sees Indian industry pick up in 96/97 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: RBI sees Indian industry pick up in 96/97 2nd half.

text.p: Indian industrial production is expected to pick up in the second half of 1996/97 (April-March), the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor said on Saturday.
"In the second half industrial production will pick up," governor Chakravarty Rangarajan told a news conference.
He said agricultural production always impacted on industrial performance. "I think about 9.0 to 10.0 (percent) industrial growth will be there," he said.

Earlier, in a letter to commercial banks, Rangarajan said the index of industrial production recorded a growth of 8.5 percent in the first quarter of 1996/97, which is much lower than the growth of 14.7 percent in the year-ago period.
Within the industrial sector, the manufacturing sector recorded a growth of 10.4 percent.

"The deceleration in the growth rate is mostly attributed to declines in the growth rates in mining and electricity. These sectors recorded very low growth of 3.6 percent and 2.2 percent respectively," Rangarajan said.
"With good rains, the generation of electricity should show improvement during the second half of the year," he said.
"Thus, on the whole, while the industrial growth will be lower than what it was in the previous year, it could nevertheless be expected to be around nine to 10.0 percent."
